question: A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?
analysis: Thymidine kinase-deficient strains of varicella-zoster virus (VZV) are resistant to acyclovir, which relies on this enzyme for activation. Famciclovir is also effective against VZV but is less commonly used than acyclovir. Ganciclovir is primarily used for cytomegalovirus infections and is not the first choice for VZV. Cidofovir is an alternative antiviral that can be used for resistant strains but is not typically the first line for VZV. Amantadine is not effective against VZV. Therefore, famciclovir would be the best option for treating shingles caused by a thymidine kinase-deficient strain of VZV.
